analysis.title: November 16: Tech Slide Drives Risk-Off
key_insights: AI-linked equities fell for a third straight session. S&P 500 -1.9%, Nasdaq -2.5%, VIX +18.7% to 22.91. IT -3.0%, Communications -2.8%, Consumer Discretionary -2.1%. Only Staples (+0.3%) and Utilities (+0.1%) rose.
Investors cut AI exposure ahead of this week's events. A new US AI-chip rule expands oversight of overseas compute rented by Chinese firms and added to pressure on the sector. Bitcoin fell 4.5%.
Treasuries twist-steepened with the belly leading (2y -1.3bp, 5y -2.2bp, 30y +0.9bp) on safe-haven demand. US 10y closed at 5.131% (-0.4bp).

Markets price 27bp of Fed hikes into the December 9 decision. SOFR options flows skewed toward additional hawkish protection. Cleveland Fed's Hammack prefers small, steady hikes but said larger moves may be needed if inflation worsens.

Fed Chair Warsh avoided comment on monetary policy. He said Fed staff are modeling scenarios in which AI lifts productivity or causes job displacement and a stock market downturn, and cautioned that the technology could disappoint.

November Empire State manufacturing index fell to 7.8 (consensus 18.0, prior 25.5), below all estimates. Prices paid eased to 45.9 from 59.5 while employment rose. MS tracks November ISM Manufacturing at 54.4 vs 55.5 in October.

The dollar firmed (DXY 103.58, +0.2%) on hawkish central bank pricing. JPY was the only G10 gainer. EUR/USD fell below 1.10 for the first time since April 2025, with 1-month risk reversals at about -0.56 vol from -0.16 on November 10.

Canada October CPI undershot (3.1% y/y vs 3.2% consensus, CPI ex food and energy 1.8% vs 2.0%). MS reads it as consistent with a BoC pause in December and a possible 25bp hike in January. USD/CAD rose 0.2% and CAD touched its weakest level since 2025. BoC Governor Macklem will not seek reappointment when his term ends in June 2027.

Euro area pricing: about 92% probability of a December ECB hike and about 57% of a further hike in March. Front-end Bunds and gilts sold off (2y +2bp and +3bp) despite lower energy prices and inflation swaps. ECB's Simkus said December alone may not be enough.

Japan Q3 GDP was negative (-0.1% q/q saar) as private consumption contracted for a second quarter. The JGB curve twist-steepened (2y 1.87%, 10y 2.885%, 30y 4.03%). USD/JPY found support around 159.35 and recovered to about 159.70. Markets are watching Governor Ueda's November 30 speech for BoJ hike clues.
Takata (BoJ) called for raising rates quickly to near the midpoint of the 1.1-2.5% neutral range, warning that low real rates could weaken the yen.

Asia tech sell-off: TAIEX fell 6% with $2.1bn of foreign equity outflows and TWD -0.4%. KOSPI fell 3.6% with $1.2bn of outflows. Taiwan's central bank has intervened more often in FX since October, and board member Chang does not rule out a pre-emptive December hike.

BRL fell about 2.27% to its weakest since April 2025 and Jan 29 DIs sold off about 24bp on doubts that Lula's fiscal package will stabilize public finances. ZAR fell a fifth straight session on coalition risk after ANC losses in municipal elections (November 27 deadline). USD/ILS rose 1.2% after Iranian drone strikes on a US air defense site in Bahrain.
China October activity missed: retail sales 0.4% y/y (consensus 0.8%), industrial production 4.8% (consensus 5.3%), fixed asset investment YTD -8.1% (consensus -7.0%).

Day ahead: US October retail sales (MS 0.0% m/m vs consensus 0.1%, control +0.2%), import prices, industrial production (MS -0.4% vs consensus +0.1%), UK labor data, German ZEW (MS 29.5 vs consensus 28.2), RBA minutes. Fed Governor Barr warned that autonomous AI agents could accelerate bank runs.
